interface.signature: def maxScoreWords(words: List[str], letters: List[str], score: List[int]) -> int:

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(w, str) and len(w) >= 1 and w.islower() and all(c.islower() for c in w) for w in words)
preconditions.description: Each word in `words` is a non-empty lowercase string with only lowercase English letters.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(l, str) and len(l) == 1 and l.islower() for l in letters)
preconditions.description: Each letter in `letters` is a single lowercase English letter.

preconditions.expression: len(score) == 26 and all(isinstance(s, int) and 0 <= s <= 10 for s in score)
preconditions.description: The `score` list has exactly 26 integers (one per lowercase letter), each between 0 and 10 inclusive.
The number of words is between 1 and 14 inclusive.
The number of letters is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(w) <= 15 for w in words)
preconditions.description: Each word in `words` has length between 1 and 15 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: return_value == max(sum(score[ord(c) - ord('a')] for c in w) for w in selected_words) if selected_words else 0 for selected_words in subsets if all(cnt[w] <= available[c] for w in selected_words for c in w for cnt in [collections.Counter(w)] for available in [collections.Counter(letters)])
postconditions.description: The function returns the maximum possible score achievable by selecting a subset of words (each used at most once) such that the total count of each letter in the selected words does not exceed the count of that letter in `letters`. The score of a word is the sum of the scores of its constituent letters.
The returned score is non-negative (0 if no valid subset exists or all words are invalid).
